children: Bharti Airtel Limited (NSE:BHARTIARTL) reported Q2FY27 revenue up 16.7% year over year and profit up 8.8% sequentially. Bharti Telecom plans near-term purchases to raise its stake above 50% from about 40%, with gradual increases over five to six years.
Previous Week Recap
Revenue Growth, Subscriber Headwinds
: Bharti Airtel reported Q2FY27 revenue up 16.7% year over year and profit up 8.8% sequentially. India mobile revenue and ARPU rose, while subscriber additions slowed and churn increased.
Bharti Telecom Plans Stake Increase

: Bharti Telecom plans near-term purchases to lift its Bharti Airtel stake above 50% from about 40%, with gradual increases over five to six years. A 10-point rise may cost $12 billion to $14 billion.
Tariff Hikes Drive ARPU Growth
: Motilal Oswal set a ₹2,400 target for Bharti Airtel, citing expected 10–15% industry tariff hikes by December or January and continued ARPU growth from premiumisation.
Shares Fall After Results
: Bharti Airtel Limited (BHARTIARTL) shares fell 1.24% to ₹2,059.60 on Monday after the company reported its second-quarter results.
Postpaid Plans Rise ₹50
: Bharti Airtel Limited (BHARTIARTL) increased monthly prices across its postpaid plans by ₹50 from October 8, raising the minimum plan price from ₹449 to ₹499.
Data-Centre And AI Expansion
: Bharti Airtel plans to expand data-centre capacity fivefold to 1GWh and develop AI models for internal use and possible third-party sales, while growing its digital, data-centre and cloud services.
Payments Bank IPO Considered
: Bharti Airtel’s payments bank may consider an IPO in three to four years after reaching targets of ₹10,000 crore in deposits and revenue, and ₹1,000 crore in profit.
Broadband Growth, FWA Pullback
: Bharti Airtel’s home broadband base rose 4.7% quarter over quarter to 15.36 million homes by end-September. Management said it was scaling back fixed wireless access-led expansion.
Vishwajeet Sinha Named Marketing VP
: Bharti Airtel Limited (BHARTIARTL) appointed Vishwajeet Sinha as Vice President of Marketing. Sinha joins from Razorpay, where his work focused on marketing and revenue growth.
